To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) is a feasible and effective treatment modality for stage I non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
stereotactic radioablation (SABR) and surgery are equally effective treatments for stage I NSCLC, but that SABR is associated with fewer adverse events and lower costs.

(i) the clinical outcome of surgically treated stage I NSCLC patients was significantly better than that of patients who received stereotactic radioablation; (ii) patients who underwent stereotactic radio-ablation showed significantly higher rates of local recurrence than those treated surgically; and (iii) patients treated with stereotactic radiation had a lower risk of death than patients who underwent surgical resection, but this finding was not statistically significant.
